implementation_strategy: Execute the preregistered paired generate–validate–repair pipeline end-to-end using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. All LLM interactions use the adapter's hosted-model API (no local models). Prompt templates and temperature/decoding fixed for determinism (temperature=0, top_p=1.0). Baseline and pipeline initial proposals are single hosted-model calls per task; pipeline repairs use the same hosted-model API with a counterexample-anchored repair prompt, bounded to ≤3 repairs per task. Relational NetKAT verifier runs inside a Docker CPU container invoked by the adapter for each parsed AST. Deterministic canonicalization and syntactic parsing convert model text → AST before verification. All retries, request/response IDs, checksums, timestamps, and hashes are logged automatically to the execution manifest. No human labour, external partners, or unavailable resources are used.
public_resources: Public intent→configuration corpus (RFC/vendor snippets + seeded synthetic topologies) — provenance hashes will be published
model_and_version_plan: Single hosted LLM accessed via hosted_netops_gvr_v1; exact runtime model identifier and provider metadata recorded per call in the execution manifest.
Prompt settings: temperature=0, top_p=1.0, deterministic max_tokens sufficient for full config. Identical prompt template for baseline and pipeline initial generation.
Repair calls: same hosted-model interface; repair prompt supplies verifier counterexample (trace), failing goal, and explicit instruction/repair budget; ≤3 repair iterations per task.
Deterministic post-processing: whitespace/token normalization, grammar whitelist enforcement, parse to ACL/ACL-like AST prior to verification.
All model-call metadata (request_id, response_id, elapsed_time, provider response hash) recorded. Adapter-level automated retries ≤2 per failed call; retries counted in logs.
task_manifest_strategy: Deterministic discovery pipeline: generate candidate intent→configuration tasks using seeded synthetic topology generators plus curated public RFC/vendor snippets (fixed RNG seed). Screen sequentially up to 400 candidates with an automated verifier-encodability test (can the task be expressed as a Relational NetKAT property and encoded). Accept the first 200 encodable tasks as the confirmatory paired set. Record SHA-256 checksums, selection seed, and provenance for every candidate; report all exclusions with checksum and reason. No manual screening.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Canonical intent→configuration prompt templates for baseline and pipeline initial proposals. Repair-prompt template: include failing verifier counterexample, failing property description, and bounded repair instruction. Deterministic canonicalization pipeline: normalize whitespace/tokens, enforce allowed-grammar token whitelist, parse into ACL-like AST. Automatic rejection rules: any output failing syntactic parse or containing out-of-grammar tokens is rejected (triggers repair prompt up to budget); outputs causing verifier runtime errors are rejected and handled per retry/exclusion rules. Secondary semantic validator: deterministic packet-trace sandbox replay for audit-sample only (Docker CPU).
execution_batches: Batch 0 — Discovery screening (deterministic): generate up to 400 candidate tasks; run automated encodability test; record encodability verdicts and exclusions. (No hosted-model calls required for screening.)

Batch 1 — Confirmatory paired runs (N=200 tasks): For each task: (a) Baseline: 1 hosted-model call → canonicalize → parse → Relational NetKAT verify. (b) Pipeline: 1 hosted-model initial proposer call → canonicalize → parse → verify; if verify fails, run up to 3 repair iterations (each = 1 hosted-model call + canonicalize+parse+verify) until verifier pass or budget exhausted. Record all outputs, ASTs, verifier logs, per-call latency and metadata. Expected model calls per task: baseline=1, pipeline initial=1, repairs average=1.0 (recommended scenario).

Batch 2 — Audit sample (deterministic 10% seed-based sample of passing configurations): for the seeded 20 tasks, run secondary semantic validation (packet-trace sandbox) in Docker CPU and automated failure-mode classification. All audit selection uses fixed RNG seed.
randomisation_plan: No randomized arm assignment (paired within-task design). All sampling and audit selections deterministic using published fixed RNG seeds. Any checksum collisions with pre-lock artifacts trigger deterministic exclusion per contamination_plan. Audit 10% sample selected with recorded seed for reproducibility.
caching_plan: Cache all model responses keyed by SHA-256 of (input + full prompt). Record cache hits in manifest. If the adapter/provider returns identical byte-level outputs across distinct inputs, automatically flag as potential provider-side caching and record for sensitivity analysis. Reuse cached verifier/AST results only when input+prompt checksum identical. Do not substitute cached outputs for fresh calls except when re-execution is a deterministic retry requirement and input+prompt checksum matches.
failure_recovery_plan: Deterministic automated retry policy: up to 2 automatic retries per failed model call (network/API). Parser or verifier runtime failures trigger repair-prompt retries under the per-task repair budget; unrecoverable syntactic or verifier runtime errors are logged and cause exclusion per preregistered exclusion rules. Tasks with unresolved technical failures after retries are logged as 'technical failure' and excluded from the confirmatory paired McNemar analysis but included in the technical-failure report. All recovery actions, timestamps, and reasons recorded in the execution manifest. No human adjudication.
result_schema: Per-task JSON record schema: {task_id, input_checksum, topology_seed, baseline:{model_call_ids[], output_text, canonicalized_text, parse_success(bool), AST|null, verifier_verdict:{pass|fail|error}, verifier_log, latency_ms}, pipeline:{initial:{model_call_id, output_text, canonicalized_text, parse_success, AST|null, verifier_verdict, verifier_log, latency_ms}, repairs:[{iteration:int, model_call_id, output_text, canonicalized_text, parse_success, AST|null, verifier_verdict, verifier_log, latency_ms}]}, final_verdict:{pass|fail|timeout|technical_failure}, repair_iterations_used:int, end_to_end_latency_ms, contamination_flags:[], hashes:{input, prompts, outputs}, semantic_audit:{audited(bool), sandbox_results|null}, provider_metadata:{model_identifier_at_runtime, provider_request_ids[]}}
estimated_compute_notes: Recommended scenario (balanced): 200 confirmatory tasks × (1 baseline call + 1 pipeline initial call + 1 average repair call) = 600 hosted-model calls. Discovery screening uses CPU verifier encodability tests (no model calls). Relational NetKAT verifier and packet-trace sandbox run in Docker on CPU. Automated retries (≤2) are logged but bounded; worst-case upper bound per preregistration is 1000 model calls (≤ maximum_planned_model_calls=10000). Wall-clock: pipeline expected to complete within the 7-day limit; typical run estimated to finish within hours to low days depending on provider latency; all timing metadata recorded.
